elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires 90 days' written notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund obligation or treatment of prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The existing bilateral provision allows either Party, including HDI, to terminate on 90 days' written notice and does not expressly restrict HDI's termination right to the end of a committed term.

elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly grants the Company, defined as Customer, a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires 90 days' written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The proviso caps the Termination Payment at the payments made to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three months preceding the Termination Date.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Although the clause gives either Party a termination right, it does not expressly require HDI's termination to be effective only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor's termination-for-convenience right requires 90 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The bilateral termination language requires either Party, including HDI, to provide 90 days' written notice.

result.reason: The redline implements most of the fallback economics by granting Customer a 90-day convenience right and capping the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 payments. It nevertheless fails the fallback because HDI's right is not expressly limited to termination effective at the end of a term. It also fails the preferred position because notice remains 90 days, no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is provided, and HDI retains an unrestricted bilateral termination right. The changes do not disturb unrelated commercial terms, but they do not complete either playbook position.
